runtimeMapping.stock: Source initial supply 1/2/3 plus potential bonus; total ready-card-inclusive capacity 2/3/4. Automatic owner skill adds one at activation and pauses SP at full stock.
runtimeMapping.operatorAttack: One Physical tracked projectile, speed15, native Attack .3s/maxAnimScale1; aerial targets allowed.
runtimeMapping.trap: Ground-only zero-slot,5DP,5s deployment cooldown. Own skill recovers8SP, remains manual, uses original Start/Idle/Die and .067s Die hit event.
runtimeMapping.detonation: S1 own tile Physical AoE/stun. S2 original x-5 cross, armed-sibling snapshot with no recursive retrigger, two zero-delta hits, shared nonstack DEF reduction5s. Owner removal cancels traps.

verificationLimits: Original graphs, selectors, transforms, templates, skill ranks and Spine events are retained. Game executable behavior is unavailable; this adapter is not native frame parity.

The UI combines the ready card and native stacked-card supply. Owner RechargeToken is bounded as immediate activation, as described by the source skill; its AnimationAbility/PassiveAttachBuff dispatch phase and native cast lock are not recovered.

Token ATK100 does not recover native host inheritance. Damage samples owner ATK including its current multiplicative modifier at placement, like existing reviewed trap adapters. Later owner modifiers do not change placed traps; atk_scale applies once as the skill description specifies.

The manual trigger requires a currently selectable ground target, following the native useTriggerInManualMode/minTarget1 components. Linked S2 dispatch bypasses that target check for armed siblings, but still requires full8SP. Compiled TriggerSkill(checkBeforeTrigger=false) internal dispatch/failed-cast ordering is not recovered.

Blast selection is evaluated at the literal .067s event using current body tiles; S2 applies its first-hit DEF debuff before its two simultaneous hits, with one shared nonstack key. Native same-frame buff/damage/withdraw dispatch order is not recovered. Traps withdraw at impact; status persists independently.

The original single trap skeleton is aliased for both facings and its Start/Idle/Die are played. Separate Unity idle, activation, blast and projectile effects/audio, modules and game frame parity are not implemented.
